transcript_context: Note the position of the iris retractor at the 6:30 position in this case. During phacoemulsification, it slips off resulting in lens subluxation posteriorly.

transcript_context: The capsular tension segment can be inserted after anterior capsulotomy and before phacoemulsification. Its design affords an extremely atraumatic insertion... transcript_context: Compared to the previous Miyake-Apple view of the capsular ring insertion, the CTS is easily and atraumatically inserted into position...The segment is secured with an iris retractor providing excellent intraoperative support as the lens is flipped and emulsified. visual_description: A double-armed 9-0 prolene suture is passed through the sclera (ab-externo technique). One needle is retrieved from the anterior chamber and passed through the fixation eyelet of the CTS. transcript_context: The CTS is designed for scleral suture fixation over an area of zonular weakness. After one end of a double-armed 9-0 prolene suture is placed to approximate the ciliary sulcus, the suture is placed through the segment fixation eyelet.

transcript_context: Here, the CTS is safely positioned over an anterior capsular tear providing adjacent capsular support and reducing traction at this site which could extend the tear. A second segment is placed and although infusion is placed in the eye, the tear does not extend.

visual_description: Following placement of a CTS in a fragile capsular bag, a three-piece IOL is implanted. The haptics are placed in the ciliary sulcus, and the central optic is then gently pushed posteriorly through the capsulorhexis opening to capture it behind the anterior capsule rim, ensuring excellent stability and centration.
transcript_context: a foldable three-piece intraocular lens is placed in the sulcus with optic capture through the capsulorhexis.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: In a case of extensive zonular weakness, a Cionni modified capsular tension ring is first inserted into the capsular bag. transcript_context: In cases of larger zonular dialysis and progressive conditions, the Cionni modified ring can be inserted in conjunction with the CTS, thus providing multipoint fixation.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: In a complex case with severe zonular weakness, iris retractors are placed on the iris to expand the pupil. A continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis is performed. A CTS is then inserted atraumatically into the capsular bag and secured with an iris retractor hooked through its fixation eyelet for stability.
transcript_context: After iris retractor assisted capsulorhexis, hydrodissection, and viscodissection, the CTS is centered over the largest area of zonular dialysis... An iris retractor secures the segment for intraoperative manipulations without concern of dislodgement.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: With the capsular bag stabilized by the CTS and iris retractors, the phaco handpiece is used to emulsify and aspirate the lens nucleus. Following this, an I/A probe is used to strip and aspirate the remaining cortical material from the capsular bag periphery.
transcript_context: Phacoemulsification is performed in a very controlled environment with the CTS in place. Compared to tension rings, cortical removal is easily stripped around the segment.

visual_description: The first CTS is temporarily removed. Double-armed sutures are passed ab-externo through the sclera. The suture is threaded through the CTS eyelet, and the CTS is re-implanted and secured by tying the suture. Due to extensive zonular weakness, a second CTS is implanted superiorly and also sutured to the sclera to provide 360-degree support.
transcript_context: In preparation for suture passage, the segment is disconnected from the iris retractor and temporarily removed from the eye. An ab-external technique is used to pass 9-0 polypropylene sutures. After passing the suture through the fixation eyelet, the CTS is re-implanted... With severe dialysis also involving the superior zonules, a second segment is implanted and sutured in this area.

visual_description: The eye is held open by a four-pronged metal speculum. A thin metallic surgical probe enters through the dilated pupil into the anterior chamber and contacts the opacified crystalline lens; fluid motion and subtle lens displacement confirm active intraocular manipulation—consistent with phacoemulsification or cortical cleanup. Small petechial hemorrhages are visible on the bulbar conjunctiva/sclera. No antibiotic delivery or tonifying activity is observed.

A blue-hubbed irrigation-aspiration handpiece with transparent tubing is inserted through a clear corneal incision into the anterior chamber. The tip is positioned near the pupillary margin and lens capsule, with visible fluid inflow and outflow. Opaque cortical material is being aspirated from the lens capsule. A speculum retracts the conjunctiva and sclera; mild episcleral bleeding is present. No nuclear fragmentation or capsulorhexis creation is observed.

A metal speculum holds the eyelids open; a fine metallic cannula enters the anterior chamber from the inferior limbus and delivers clear irrigating fluid, causing visible dispersion and partial washout of fresh blood from the iris surface and surrounding stroma. The crystalline lens remains centered and shows slight oscillation with fluid flow. Anterior chamber depth is maintained, though residual blood remains inferiorty and near the limbus.

visual_description: Two McCool capsular retractors are inserted through limbal incisions and hooked onto the edge of the capsulorhexis to stabilize the superior aspect of the capsular bag where zonular dehiscence is most apparent.
transcript_context: And so we placed McCool capsular retractors, part of the IMPEX McCool cataract support system. These are similar to iris retractors except they hold the capsule...

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: After discovering more extensive zonular loss, two additional McCool capsular retractors are placed inferiorly, providing 360-degree support to the entire capsular bag.
transcript_context: We find there's also loss of zonules that develops from about 2 o'clock to 5:30 on the screenshot so we placed an additional two McCool capsular support system retractors.

visual_description: After removing the remaining nuclear fragments, a vitrectomy probe is used to perform irrigation, aspiration, and anterior vitrectomy due to vitreous prolapse. The surgeon decides to remove the entire unstable capsular bag complex, rendering the eye aphakic.
transcript_context: We are able to remove all of the cataract and we begin irrigation and aspiration using the vitrectomy because vitreous had presented itself around the equator of the bag.

visual_description: A vitrectomy probe is used in an I/A (irrigation/aspiration) mode to thoroughly remove the viscoelastic substance from the anterior chamber, from both in front of and behind the ACIOL.
transcript_context: We then remove the viscoelastic that was placed into the eye to complete the operation with our vitrectomy.

visual_description: The surgeon stabilizes the globe with a fixation instrument. A keratome is used to create a shallow initial groove at the superotemporal limbus, causing minor bleeding from limbal vessels. The keratome is then re-introduced and advanced through the corneal stroma to create a tunnel. The angle of the blade is adjusted, steepening to penetrate Descemet's membrane and enter the anterior chamber. The full width of the blade enters the AC, and the instrument is then smoothly withdrawn.
transcript_context: a little light groove is made right at that gray line. Now the keratome is positioned appropriately... the blade then changes angle, aiming somewhat towards the corneal apex. And then here at the end, a little more angle change in entering the eye, all the way in, all the way out.

visual_description: Immediately following the trabeculotomy, blood refluxes from the Schlemm's canal area and begins to fill the anterior chamber, forming a significant hyphema.
transcript_context: Oh, a little bit of bleeding here.

visual_description: An irrigation cannula is inserted through a paracentesis to infuse balanced salt solution, increasing the intraocular pressure to tamponade the bleeding source in the angle.
transcript_context: You get the pressure up is what I do. Yeah. Get the IOP up in the eye right now.

visual_description: A prolonged and meticulous process of removing the large blood clot is undertaken. Microforceps are used to grasp and pull out large pieces of the clot. An I/A or phaco probe is used bimanually with a manipulator to aspirate smaller fragments and dissect the clot away from the iris and angle structures.
transcript_context: Okay, micro forceps maybe you can grab that clot and yank it out. That can work too.

visual_description: A slit lamp examination on the first day after surgery shows the eye's condition. A small, layered hyphema remains inferiorly, and there is some fibrin on the IOL surface, but the cornea is relatively clear and the anterior chamber is formed.
transcript_context: So here we go, post-op day one. Ah, a little bit of blood still there, a little bit of a uh fibrin in there but the patient will be fine.

visual_description: A hydrodissection cannula is inserted under the anterior capsule, and fluid is injected to separate the lens cortex from the capsule. During the procedure, the pupil begins to constrict, and the iris tissue shows signs of prolapsing through the primary incision.
transcript_context: Here we go. Starting out with a routine case, we're beginning our hydrodissection. And all we notice is the pupil is just a little smaller...but then we get the suggestion that there's going to be a little bit of tendency toward iris prolapse.

visual_description: Due to persistent iris prolapse at the original primary incision, the surgeon closes it with a nylon suture. A new clear corneal incision is then created 90 degrees away to provide a stable entry port for the remainder of the surgery.
transcript_context: We have iris prolapse again...We choose to move 90 degrees away from our initial primary incision that has now been sutured...

visual_description: An anterior vitrectomy cutter is inserted into the eye through the new incision. It cuts and aspirates prolapsed vitreous strands from the anterior chamber and pupillary space. The remaining remnants of the capsular bag are also removed to clear the visual axis completely.
transcript_context: We do an anterior vitrectomy. We essentially take out the capsular bag.

visual_description: A post-operative slit lamp examination of the patient's eye. The view shows a clear cornea, a stable and well-centered diffractive optic IOL (Symfony lens), and a reformed, quiet anterior chamber. The irregular pupil shape from the previous iris trauma is visible.
transcript_context: And then this is the patient's appearance on post-op day number one...a very well centered symphony implant.

visual_description: A cannula is used to inject cohesive viscoelastic, inflating the capsular bag and filling the anterior chamber in preparation for IOL implantation.
transcript_context: I find that if we vacuum out this viscoelastic near the angle now, when I re-fill the eye here with the cohesive viscoelastic, it has less of an effect of pushing that earlier viscoelastic into the angle.

visual_description: The video opens with a close-up view of an eye with a severely dislocated crystalline lens, which is tilted vertically and partially visible in the anterior chamber. The pupil is widely dilated and fixed. The conjunctiva is hyperemic with prominent blood vessels.
transcript_context: The patient suffers severe blunt trauma with uh very significant crystalline lens dislocation as you can see, barely hanging on with a couple of zonules sitting vertically in the anterior vitreous cavity. Atonic fixed pupil and traumatic glaucoma with a very high pressure of 50 millimeters of mercury.

visual_description: A cannula is inserted into the anterior chamber to inject triamcinolone, which appears as a white, cloudy substance that stains the prolapsed vitreous. A vitrectomy cutter is then introduced through the pars plana trocar, and an anterior vitrectomy is performed, clearing the white-stained vitreous from the anterior chamber and anterior vitreous cavity.
transcript_context: Some uh triamcinolone will be used here to identify vitreous, some of which is prolapsed in the anterior chamber... Using an anterior infusion and pars plana cutter insertion, we're able to evacuate the anterior segment and the anterior vitreous cavity of vitreous with uh appropriate vitrectomy.

transcript_context: And then using phaco chop techniques, we'll basically create a central crack and then hemi-flip each of the heminuclei.

visual_description: Using a bimanual setup with separate irrigation and aspiration handpieces (identified as vitrectomy instruments), the surgeon removes the remaining soft lens cortex from the capsular bag, leaving the bag clean.

visual_description: A scleral groove is created. The surgeon passes a 25-gauge needle through the scleral groove, under the iris, and into the anterior chamber. A double-armed 7-0 Gore-Tex suture, previously threaded through a CTS eyelet, is docked into the needle and externalized. The process is repeated for the second arm of the suture and for the second CTS on the opposite side. A slip knot is created externally for later tension adjustment.
transcript_context: This is a scleral groove made tangential to the limbus... 25 gauge hypodermic needle is used in through the scleral groove under the iris above the capsular bag to dock a double armed 7-0 Goretex suture which has been threaded through the eyelet centrally of the segment.

visual_description: A capsular tension ring (CTR) injector is inserted into the anterior chamber. The CTR is then carefully injected and guided into the capsular bag, where it expands to provide circumferential support to the bag and zonules.
transcript_context: in order to prevent a repeat Z syndrome, we elect to place a capsular tension ring to expand the capsular bag and prevent it from contracting in an abnormal way.

visual_description: A Sinskey hook is used to dial and center the new IOL within the capsular bag. It is observed that one of the haptics has subluxated into the anterior chamber. Micro-scissors are re-introduced to amputate this malpositioned haptic, which is then removed from the eye.
transcript_context: Once the lens has been positioned, we then find that one of the haptics is now subluxing into the anterior chamber, so we amputate this haptic...

Here, look at that, moving it out of the angle. So goniosynechialysis at the slit lamp with a 30 gauge needle...

transcript_context: GSL WITH IA TIP. AYYALA TECHNIQUE...Using the eye probe to gently grab the iris with the tip and pull it centrally.

The needle is then externalized through a separate paracentesis. The process is shown for both the superior and inferior haptics, capturing each one with a suture pass.
transcript_context: We use a 10-0 nylon suture on a long needle... We do the same thing for the inferior haptic here.

transcript_context: We then elected to use a stabilized capsular tension ring... We inserted this capsular tension ring into the bag after we had taken out probably about half of the cataract.

transcript_context: So once we have inserted the capsular tension ring, we're able to have a more stable capsular bag which allows me to safely remove the remainder of this cataract.

visual_description: A 27-gauge needle is used to puncture the posterior capsule behind the IOL optic. Viscoelastic is injected behind the capsule to separate it from the anterior hyaloid face. Microforceps are then inserted to create a continuous circular tear in the posterior capsule.
transcript_context: Here we're using a 27-gauge needle with viscoelastic. Here we're going to puncture the posterior capsule, place the bevel into the Burger space and inject viscoelastic... This is a micro forceps here, used to propagate the capsular rhexis.

This secures the optic behind both the anterior and posterior capsule remnants, a technique known as buttonholing or posterior optic capture.
transcript_context: we can now place this lens in a posterior optic buttonhole position without vitrectomy here... the plastic of the optic will prevent that from going in the central visual axis and there's no need to do vitrectomy.

transcript_context: There's the nucleus being pierced by the 27-gauge needle here, aspirating out some of that liquefied lens cortex. ... there's the rocking of the nucleus. I like it.

visual_description: To protect the posterior capsule during removal of the last nuclear fragment, a dispersive viscoelastic is injected behind the piece, creating a protective barrier (Viscoshell). The sharp chopper is exchanged for a blunt spatula-like instrument (Becker device). This instrument manipulates the last fragment and shields the posterior capsule as the phaco probe emulsifies and aspirates the remaining nuclear material.
transcript_context: For that last fragment removal, this risk of course of post-occlusion surge and posterior capsule rupture, we're using a dispersive viscoelastic placed behind the lens material... and converting from a chopping second instrument to more of a blunt spatula like device here...

Each half is then brought to the iris plane, further sub-chopped into smaller fragments, and emulsified. The pupil constricts during this process.

visual_description: A Cionni-type capsular tension segment (CTS), a hemi-ring device, is inserted into the capsular bag using forceps. Both eyelets of the CTS are tucked under the anterior capsular rim in the area of greatest zonular weakness.
transcript_context: And now the capsular tension segment is used. This is a coat hanger-like device, a hemi-ring. Both islets are placed under the anterior capsule.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: An iris hook is inserted upside-down through a paracentesis and hooked through the central eyelet of the CTS. This provides temporary external support to the CTS and the area of zonular weakness during lensectomy.
transcript_context: The central islet will be used in conjunction with an iris hook, which we place upside down through the islet. And this provides really broad support in the area where the zonules are weak.

visual_description: The supporting iris hook is removed, and the CTS is maneuvered from the capsular bag into the anterior chamber. A scleral incision is made externally. A 25-gauge needle is passed through the scleral incision into the anterior chamber. A 7-0 Gore-Tex suture is threaded through the needle tip (docking technique) and then passed through the eyelet of the CTS. Both ends of the suture now exit through the scleral incision.
transcript_context: Now the CTS is now mobilized... and we will plan for suture placement... using a 7-0 Gore-Tex suture here in an ab-externo docking technique to place it through the CTS.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: Using two pairs of forceps, the surgeon ties the external Gore-Tex suture ends into a slip knot. This allows for adjustable tension to be applied to the CTS and capsular bag later in the procedure.
transcript_context: As we see, the CTS is being tied in a slip knot here. A slip knot is important because we don't want to place too much tension on the device yet.

visual_description: The surgeon attempts to polish the posterior capsule using the I/A tip. Gentle pressure from the tip, even without aspiration, causes the fragile posterior capsule to tear, resulting in a posterior capsule rupture.
transcript_context: The capsule opens with gentle pressure from the I/A tip without aspiration

visual_description: To manage the rupture, a viscoelastic cannula is used to inject a dispersive viscoelastic (OcuCoat) followed by a cohesive viscoelastic (Healon GV) into the anterior chamber and capsular bag. This stabilizes the eye and provides a tamponade effect on the posterior capsule opening to prevent vitreous prolapse.
transcript_context: So we fill the eye with viscoelastic, first OcuCoat and then secondly Healon GV to tamponade the posterior capsule...

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: A vitrectomy probe is inserted into the anterior chamber to remove prolapsed vitreous and residual lens material. A second instrument manipulates the lens capsule. This is performed due to extensive zonular dialysis indicated by the red arrow.
transcript_context: ...zonular dialysis requiring a vitrectomy initially to remove vitreous from the anterior segment.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: A capsular tension ring (CTR) is injected into the capsular bag. A manipulator is used to guide the trailing end of the CTR fully into the bag, providing circumferential support to the equator.
transcript_context: A capsular tension ring is placed in the bag...

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: A capsular tension segment (CTS) is placed inside the capsular bag at the location of the zonular dialysis. A long needle carrying a Gore-Tex suture is passed through the sclera, through the eyelet of the CTS, and then externalized, securing the CTS and the entire capsular bag to the scleral wall.
transcript_context: ...followed by the placement of a capture tension segment which is sutured to the sclera in the area of the zonular dialysis with 7-0 Goretex suture.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: A metal fixation ring is placed onto the surface of the globe to provide counter-traction and stabilize the eye.
transcript_context: So place the fixation ring to hold the globe.

visual_description: A cannula is used to hydrate the corneal incisions to ensure they are sealed. The final view shows the IOL well-centered in the capsular bag, but the view of the posterior segment is obscured by the persistent milky fluid in the vitreous cavity.
transcript_context: I think I would just finish the case like this as a cataract surgeon and refer the patient to a vitreoretinal colleague probably for a full vitrectomy. I just don't want that big inflammatory load in the vitreous cavity.

anomalies.category: Pupil Constriction / Iris Suturing / Sphincterotomy / Synechia

transcript_context: A Kugelhook is used to identify the areas of posterior synechiae which are fairly extensive and fairly strong. You can see with the Kugelhook it is difficult right now to dissect off the iris from the anterior capsule.

anomalies.category: Pupil Constriction / Iris Suturing / Sphincterotomy / Synechia

visual_description: A Kugelhook is used to further dissect the firm posterior synechiae connecting the iris to the anterior capsule rim. Viscoelastic is injected to assist in the separation of tissues.
transcript_context: Again the Kugelhook is used. We have some further dissection of the iris from the anterior capsule.

anomalies.category: Pupil Constriction / Iris Suturing / Sphincterotomy / Synechia

visual_description: A bimanual technique is employed to release the tenacious synechiae. Microforceps grasp and stabilize the iris, providing counter-traction while a Kugelhook dissects the adhesions from the anterior capsule.
transcript_context: And here we're using a pair of micro forceps to hold the iris while we're using a Kugelhook to release the synechiae. This is an effective strategy when the synechiae is fairly firm.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: Capsulorhexis forceps are introduced into the anterior chamber to grasp and remove the free-floating capsular disc created by the laser. The entire lens and capsular bag are seen to move significantly, indicating extreme zonular weakness.
transcript_context: Oh my goodness, look how much it moves. There is just no capsule support here.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: Five capsule support hooks (iris hooks) are inserted through the paracentesis incisions. The hooks are carefully engaged with the edge of the capsulotomy to stabilize the entire capsular bag.
transcript_context: Yeah, you definitely need capsule hooks here. So here comes some capsule hooks... And then this is all that's supporting the lens capsule or bag now.

visual_description: Triamcinolone acetonide is injected into the anterior chamber, staining the vitreous strands white. A vitrectomy cutter and an infusion line are used to perform an anterior vitrectomy, clearing the vitreous from the anterior segment and incision sites.
transcript_context: So here at this point, yeah, capsule bag is out, I'd put some triamcinolone. Exactly what I would do. Small gauge, 23-gauge vitrectomy here. Look, there's already some vitreous to the wound.

visual_description: As the last nuclear fragment is removed, a viscoelastic cannula is introduced through a paracentesis to inject viscoelastic into the anterior chamber, specifically under the main incision, to prevent iris prolapse as the phaco probe is withdrawn.
transcript_context: Before coming out of the eye, we're placing some viscoelastic under the incision just to keep the iris back...

anomalies.category: Pupil Constriction / Iris Suturing / Sphincterotomy / Synechia

visual_description: A second paracentesis is created with a side-port blade. A spatula is then inserted through the new incision and swept 360 degrees between the iris and the anterior lens capsule to break posterior synechiae.
transcript_context: [00:36 - 00:44]: And now another paracentesis. Okay. And you may want to go with a spatula and kind of break those synechiae. Exactly. Well, synechiolysis there, 360.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

transcript_context: [01:11 - 01:18]: And the surgeon here is going to try to use, there you go, a B-Hex ring. This is a pupil expansion ring, placing it inside the eye. And look at that. It breaks.

transcript_context: [01:39 - 01:47]: But in this case, the surgeon is going to elect to do some mini iris sphincterotomies using micro scissors to make multiple small cuts here at the pupil sphincter.

visual_description: After filling the anterior chamber with viscoelastic, capsulorhexis forceps are used to create a continuous circular opening in the anterior capsule. The surgeon initiates the tear by pinching the central capsule, creating a flap, and guiding it circumferentially to create a round, well-centered capsulorhexis.
transcript_context: We'll make our capsulorhexis here, pinching in with the forceps and just closing them and we can start tearing around rhexis here... we want to create a nice round five to five and a half millimeter capsulorhexis, which is centered in the patient's visual axis

visual_description: A cohesive viscoelastic is injected into the eye using a cannula, first filling and expanding the capsular bag to create space for the IOL, and then filling the anterior chamber to maintain space and protect the corneal endothelium.
transcript_context: Of course now fill our capsular bag with our viscoelastic. This is the cohesive viscoelastic going inside the eye.

visual_description: In an eye with a significant hyphema, a needle is used to create a paracentesis and inject a large air bubble into the superior anterior chamber. transcript_context: A big air bubble, a gas bubble in the eye, just air. That's going to help put some pressure now. And now you can drain it... and get some of this blood out. And now you can slowly aspirate some of that.

anomalies.category: Pupil Constriction / Iris Suturing / Sphincterotomy / Synechia

The needle tip is used to perform synechialysis, breaking adhesions between the iris and the lens at the pupillary margin. The needle is then used for goniosynechialysis, sweeping the peripheral iris away from the iridocorneal angle.
transcript_context: Now, here's using the needle to pull the iris out of the angle. That's, be careful doing this. This is the goniosynechialysis with a 30-gauge needle.

The surgeon uses two micro-instruments (choppers/manipulators) to bimanually crack the nucleus along the sculpted grooves. During this maneuver, significant zonular weakness becomes evident as the capsular bag equator is visible from the 9 to 12 o'clock position.
transcript_context: After we've created our two grooves, we find that there's a posterior plate that is difficult to crack. But in the process of cracking the lens we see from 9 o'clock until 12 o'clock in the video that the equator of the bag is visible, indicating loss of zonular integrity in that area.

A long needle with polypropylene suture is passed through the sclera, through the segment's eyelet, and then externalized. A second pass is made for the other end of the suture. visual_description: The surgeon performs a final visual inspection, confirming the IOL is now well-centered and planar. The anterior chamber maintainer is removed from the eye, and the corneal incisions are hydrated to ensure they are sealed.

We close the incisions and as we're looking at the eye, we kind of think to ourselves, hey, if this was my eye, I'd be completely satisfied with the position and orientation of this implant.

visual_description: A cannula is used to inject balanced salt solution into the stromal sides of the main corneal incision. This hydration causes the tissue to swell, ensuring a watertight seal. A small amount of prolapsed iris is pushed back into the eye.
transcript_context: And now it's time to seal up the incisions here. ... little iris prolapse, we'll push that back in the eye... and a little bit more hydration of the incision.

visual_description: A capsular tension ring (CTR) is injected into the capsular bag. A Sinskey hook is used to guide the CTR fully into the equatorial fornix of the bag, which helps to expand and stabilize it.
transcript_context: We've now cleared the capsular bag, we'll keep the AC formed with viscoelastic, the capsular tension ring is used, CTR here, and this will round out the capsular bag...

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: A partial-thickness scleral groove is created with a blade near the limbus, in the area corresponding to the zonular dialysis.
transcript_context: One and a half millimeters back from the posterior edge of that blue zone is where we make our groove.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: A capsular tension segment (CTS) is placed into the capsular bag. A 7-0 GORE-TEX suture is passed from outside the eye (ab externo) through the scleral groove using a 25-gauge needle for docking. The suture is threaded through the CTS eyelet and externalized, preparing it for fixation to the scleral wall.
transcript_context: This is the capsular tension segment being placed here, and we're going to use 7-0 GORE-TEX... using a docking approach, ab externo with the 25 gauge needle... this will support that bag long term with GORE-TEX suture.

anomalies.category: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion

visual_description: Using two pairs of microforceps, the surgeon ties the externalized GORE-TEX suture to fixate the CTS to the scleral wall. The suture knot is then trimmed and carefully buried into the previously created scleral groove. The final view shows a well-centered IOL and artificial iris complex.
transcript_context: Finally, we will lock that suture in place and bury the knot...
